study_identification_part.si_4_title: Comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Two datasets were used: (1) developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) - an open-access project providing preterm- to term-born control neonates for normative modeling; (2) Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) study - a single-site clinical research cohort at St Thomas' Hospital/Evelina Children's Hospital, London, providing neonates with Down syndrome. Note: dHCP is classified as HCP-D (Human Connectome Project Development) as it focuses on the developing human brain. The eBiDS is classified as SINGLE-SITE as it is a single institutional cohort without a standardized dataset name.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "A total of 493 preterm- to term-born neonates [...] were selected from the dHCP (www.developingconnectome.org) [...] for normative modeling of brain tissue volumes from 32 to 46 weeks PMA at scan."; "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited from the neonatal unit and postnatal wards at St Thomas' Hospital London and invited for a neonatal scan"; "The dHCP is an open-access project. The imaging data used in this study were included in the third dHCP data release (2021)"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: FukamiGartner2023.pdf.md: Participants / Preterm- and term-born neonates for normative modeling, L63-66; Participants / Neonates with DS, L59-62; Data availability, L97-99

answer.HCP-D (dHCP): normative modeling (training reference population for GPR model)

answer.SINGLE-SITE (eBiDS): clinical research (independent sample for deviation quantification in Down syndrome)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The dHCP control sample (n=493) was used as the reference population for Gaussian process regression (GPR) normative modeling of brain tissue volumes from 32 to 46 weeks PMA. The eBiDS sample of neonates with DS (n=25) was used as the independent clinical sample to extract individualized volumetric z-scores (deviations from normative mean).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "We used a robust cross-sectional sample of 493 preterm- to term-born control neonates from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) to perform normative modeling of regional brain tissue volumes from 32 to 46 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) at scan. Deviation from the normative mean was quantified in 25 neonates with DS [...] from the Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) study"

model-1.model-name: GPR-based volumetric normative model (Gaussian process regression)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using Gaussian process regression (GPR) on 493 control neonates from the dHCP. The study does not distinguish between train/validation/test splits within the control sample - the entire sample was used as the reference population for normative modeling. No separate train phase N is reported.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "A total of 493 preterm- to term-born neonates [243 female, 86 preterm births < 37 weeks GA, of which 33 were born < 32 GA, PMA at scan median (range) = 41.00 (31.14-45.14) weeks] were selected from the dHCP (www.developingconnectome.org) (Edwards et al. 2022) for normative modeling of brain tissue volumes from 32 to 46 weeks PMA at scan."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age information is provided for PMA (postmenstrual age) at scan, not gestational age at birth, as this is the primary age variable used for normative modeling. The control group GA at birth median was 39.86 weeks (IQR: 38.14-40.71, range: 24.71-43.00 weeks). Mean and SD are not directly reported but median and range are clearly stated for PMA at scan. No train/test split is used - the entire 493 subjects serve as the normative reference.
